perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith and Elizabeth are colleagues at a construction company: Keith is a construction worker, Elizabeth is the receptionist. They have a friendly but professional relationship, usually interacting when Keith comes to the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him over a few days. He wondered whether he had unknowingly upset her or caused a misunderstanding.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. Elizabeth said no, not at all, and explained she was dealing with personal stuff and was sorry if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic after hearing this was not about anger toward him. He offered to listen if she needed someone to talk to and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth thanked him and agreed it sounded good.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses, which Keith perceived as severe. Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective could sometimes help. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith observed Elizabeth becoming slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her or overstepped, and he felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and reassured her he was there to support her no matter what. Elizabeth said he did not overstep, appreciated his concern, and said it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He told her he was glad they could talk and that he was always there if she needed to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him now. He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.

Keith has no direct knowledge of Elizabeth’s private thoughts or personal circumstances beyond what she said and what he observed in their interactions.
